text: Gold fell below $3,800 an ounce for the first time since September 2025, down about 1.4% by early Wednesday as traders priced in a December Fed rate hike.
Silver dropped about 3.2% to near $45.75, its lowest in over a year, falling harder than gold.
Nasdaq-100 futures rose roughly 0.75–1.2% and S&P 500 futures 0.3–0.7% after Nvidia's quarterly revenue and outlook beat forecasts; QQQ traded near $662 before the open.
Nvidia shares rose about 3% before the open on its results, lifting other AI-related stocks.
Brent crude slipped about 1% to $92.14 after an industry report showed a large build in US crude stocks.
The 10-year Treasury yield edged down 1 bp to about 5.09% ahead of the Fed minutes, with futures markets pricing roughly a 95% chance of a December hike.
Bitcoin held near $64,150, a little above Tuesday's close, with crypto sentiment still at extreme fear.
